features.statement: Document title combines site names with a tagline separated by an en dash.
Page uses a single h1 hero headline split across two lines with a line break.
Layout uses several section elements plus header, nav and footer but no main landmark.
Two typefaces: a humanist sans for body/UI text and a heavy condensed display face for headings.
Hero headline is two-colored, white and yellow, with a colored offset drop shadow.
Headings pair a small eyebrow phrase above a much larger display word, repeated across sections.
Navigation and headings are set almost entirely in uppercase.
Extreme type scale contrast: huge display headings against small body copy and labels, few intermediate sizes.
Text is mostly white on dark or photo backgrounds, with pale blue as secondary text color.
A single yellow accent is used for primary CTAs, eyebrow headings and footer column titles.
Section backgrounds alternate in bold bands of yellow, navy, cyan, red and tinted photos, giving strong vertical rhythm.
Dark navy header bar with logo left and nav links plus second logo right.
Full-width yellow alert banner at top with heading, text and a dismiss × button.
Hero is split 50/50 into two equal full-height photos, each with logo and label overlaid at lower left.
Photos are tinted with colored overlays, such as blue or red washes, over full-bleed backgrounds.
Row of three white rounded quick-link cards with solid colored bottom-edge shadow on a colored band.
CTA pairs combine a filled yellow pill with an outlined white pill button.
Pill radii used for buttons while most other elements have square corners and no small radii.
Flat styling without gradients, backdrop blur or animations; only simple transitions.
Footer is dark with four columns, each headed by a yellow uppercase title over pale link lists.
Content sits in a centered fixed-width container narrower than the viewport.
Image pair with hand-lettered stencil graphic card beside a rounded photo, unevenly aligned.
All images carry alt attributes, with empty alt for decorative images.
Calls to action are implemented as anchors rather than buttons.
Class names are semantic and custom rather than utility-style.
Notices such as closures and delays are stated in plain, direct sentences.
